name: RUSSIA

flag.title: Russian Tricolour
flag.note: White, blue & red — since Peter the Great

lead: Russia has eleven time zones. When kids in Moscow eat breakfast, children near the Pacific coast are going to bed. It holds the world's deepest lake and enough land to fit the USA nearly twice.

facts.label: Land area
facts.sub: Largest country on Earth by area

sections.wows: 7 things to make you go wow

geo: Russia covers one-eighth of the land on Earth. The Ural Mountains divide Europe from Asia. Beyond them lies the Siberian taiga, the planet's largest forest.
Lake Baikal holds about one-fifth of Earth's unfrozen fresh water. It plunges 1,642 m deep. Kamchatka in the far east has more than 160 volcanoes, and about 29 are active.
animals: The Amur tiger, the world's largest wild cat, prowls the birch forests. The brown bear is Russia's unofficial national animal. Bears outnumber tigers by tens of thousands.
The Arctic fox's coat turns pure white in winter to hide on the snowy tundra. The nerpa is a seal that lives only in Lake Baikal.
culture: The Bolshoi Ballet has wowed audiences for 250 years. Tchaikovsky gave the world Swan Lake. Matryoshka nesting dolls are among the world's best-known crafts.
Borscht is beetroot soup. Blini are thin pancakes. Pelmeni are dumplings. Tea from a samovar is the heart of any gathering.
history: Russia began as medieval Slavic city-states. Ivan the Terrible became the first tsar in 1547. Peter the Great built St Petersburg from scratch.
A revolution in 1917 created the Soviet Union. In 1957, it launched Sputnik, the first satellite. In 1961, Yuri Gagarin became the first human in space. The USSR broke up in 1991.
wows: Russia has 11 time zones, more than almost any other country.
Lake Baikal alone holds 20% of the world's unfrozen fresh water.
The Trans-Siberian Railway is Earth's longest, at 9,289 km.
Yuri Gagarin became the first human in space in April 1961.
Russia has 32 UNESCO World Heritage Sites, including the Kremlin.
People call Siberia's taiga the lungs of the planet.
Moscow's chandelier-lit metro stations are nicknamed 'the people's palace'.

myths.myth: Russia is always frozen and covered in snow
myths.fact: Moscow hits 25°C in July, and the Black Sea coast is a popular beach spot.

myths.myth: Bears roam the streets of Russian cities
myths.fact: Brown bears live in remote forests, far from cities. City Russians see more pigeons than bears.
